parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime pairs enforced criminalisation of same-sex conduct — reaching a trans visitor whose relationship reads as same-sex, with a 15-year hard-labour sentence demonstrably served in 2024 — with police as perpetrators: documented violence, prolonged detentions, bribe extortion (fines raised 500→15,000 units), and forced anal examinations used as court evidence in a mass trial, condemned as torture. Society is hostile (2% moral acceptance in 2010; 2022 presidential statement sparking hate speech and assaults; mob attacks including police officers). Recourse is illusory: one contested 2013 acquittal, no protections, assembly barred. Entry/document rules are unsourced, but discovery leads to imprisonment and degrading custody, not merely exclusion.

entry_documents.exposure: No entry, visa, passport or gender-marker rules sourced. Document mismatch or any discovery of trans status can feed police scrutiny; a relationship read as same-sex falls squarely within enforced penal provisions.
entry_documents.interaction: Border or hotel document checks can trigger identification → police involvement → criminal process under sodomy provisions; no sourced safeguard interrupts this chain.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented: prolonged LGBTQI+ detentions, police violence, bribery after arrest, threatened additional charges to extort payment ($30–$900), forced anal examinations as evidence (mass trial of ~20 men), 15-year hard-labour sentence served by 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: One 2013 freedom-of-expression acquittal (Magistrate and High Court), contested by government; no shown custody protections.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Outing during any encounter converts into arrest → extortion or prosecution → custodial placement with torture-level examination practice.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Facility placement rules for trans detainees not documented; forced anal examinations occur in state medical custody. Penal code §158(3) shows asymmetric same-sex offences reaching children, relevant to a travelling minor.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: A detained visitor enters the same custodial system that conducts examinations; no placement safeguard is sourced for a minor either.

care_services.exposure: No broad healthcare anti-discrimination protection; documented inability of LGBTQI+ people to access services; HIV programmes exclude same-sex relationships. No trans-specific care information at all.
care_services.protection: 2014 health-professions Code of Ethics bars discrimination on sexuality grounds; 2022 HIV guidelines require serving adolescents regardless of orientation — narrow, sexuality-framed, not gender-identity-framed.
care_services.interaction: Emergency care requiring disclosure risks outing into a police-linked system; the narrow codes do not shield a trans visitor from criminal exposure.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: State threat-framing documented: president's 30 May 2022 statement opposing LGBTQ protections sparked hate-speech and assault spike; no credible efforts to rescind discriminatory laws; expression/assembly on LGBTQ matters non-existent; anti-LGBTQ NGO operating since 1999.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: 2013 court ruling recognising expressive rights (contested, not shown applied since); 2015 adolescent policy naming gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing licenses both police extortion and mob action; police officers joined a 2015 mob attack.

minors_guardians.exposure: §158(3) penal code criminalises same-sex gross indecency among children with no opposite-sex parallel; a minor travelling with a trans guardian enters the same hostile societal and policing climate (mob violence documented).
minors_guardians.protection: Community service/counselling framing in §158(3); 2022 HIV guidelines require serving adolescents regardless of behaviour.
minors_guardians.interaction: Family outing or any disclosure can expose both the parent's relationship (read as same-sex → imprisonment) and the child under an asymmetric offence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Documented pattern: 2014 mob apprehension of suspected lesbians; 2015 mob attack on gay man including three police officers; advocacy reports of pervasive societal violence; 2022 spike after presidential statement. Police are a source of risk, not protection.
street_violence_police_response.protection: No documented police protection; 'no credible reports of government agents condoning violence' is a thin, offsetting note.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: A trans visitor identified as LGBTQ can face mob or police action with no functioning complaint route.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Recourse thin: LGBTQ organisation registration refused in principle; expression/assembly non-existent; government contested the sole favourable judgment; recent violence incidents (post-2022) and current exam practice unrecorded — unknown, not safe.
remedies_unknowns.protection: 2013 High Court acquittal precedent exists on paper.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: A traveller cannot realistically litigate or complain during a short stay; uncertainty compounds exposure rather than mitigating it.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar: enforced criminal statute, routine arrest on document/appearance mismatch, illusory remedies despite formal rights, no credible execution. This dossier adds forced anal examinations (torture-grade custody harm) and a actually-served long sentence, but lacks Varnalia's capital clause — net comparable.

Lower: 0.25-A involves fines, rare imprisonment and overturned convictions. Here imprisonment is documented as ongoing (2024), torture-level examinations are used as evidence, and police themselves perpetrate violence — a heavier, state-linked exposure than raids and shakedowns.

Materially lower: 0.35-A's register excludes and humiliates without arrest or criminal charge. This dossier's traveller faces criminal prosecution, years of hard labour, forced examinations and police extortion — custody with torture risk, not administrative exclusion.

Far lower: 0.55-B's worst outcomes are discretionary secondary screening, refused admission and missed connections. This dossier combines enforced criminalisation, state-perpetrated abuse and hostile society — a different severity universe.

parsed.synthesis: Every operative layer aligns against the traveller: enforced criminalisation reaches relationships read as same-sex; police convert any discovery into detention, extortion or prosecution, with forced anal examinations documented as evidence in a mass trial; society is hostile and a 2022 head-of-state statement modelled that hostility; remedies are a single contested 2013 acquittal against a documented bar on advocacy. Unsourced entry rules create uncertainty, but discovery routes into the criminal-justice system, whose severity (imprisonment with hard labour, degradingcustodial practices) governs. The narrow health codes are sexuality-framed and cannot offset criminal exposure. Travelling with a minor adds the asymmetric §158(3) offence. Worst documented feature: tier-2 state-tolerated targeting plus enforced criminalisation → 0.15.
